1.title: Are close-knit families a thing of the past?
1.brief: Write an opinion essay answering the question: “Are close-knit families disappearing in modern society?” Give arguments for both sides and your conclusion.
1.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre si las familias unidas están desapareciendo, con argumentos y conclusión.
criteria: Five verbs followed by gerunds (avoid, keep, miss, consider, can’t help).
Two noun clauses after “be” (The problem is that…, What matters is whether…).
Four paragraphs with an introduction, two sides and a conclusion.
1.model:
Many people claim that the close-knit family is disappearing. In Colombia, where families have traditionally been large and united, this question is particularly relevant.

On the one hand, modern life makes staying close difficult. Young people often consider moving to big cities or abroad for work, and parents keep working long hours. Many grandparents miss seeing their grandchildren every Sunday. The problem is that technology can replace real contact: a video call is not the same as a family lunch.

On the other hand, families have not stopped caring; they have simply changed. Siblings who live in different countries keep chatting every day on WhatsApp, and many couples avoid moving far from their parents so that they can help with childcare. The truth is that bonding with relatives now takes different forms.

In conclusion, I believe that families are not drifting apart but adapting. What matters is whether we make an effort to be present. I can't help thinking that a family that shares one meal a week is still a close-knit family.

1.title: Patching things up
1.brief: Write an email to a relative or friend after an argument. Apologise, explain your feelings and suggest how to patch things up.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un familiar o amigo después de una discusión: discúlpate y propón cómo reconciliarse.
criteria: Four verbs + gerund, including after a preposition (sorry for shouting, insist on paying).
One noun clause after “be” (The thing is that…).
Use two expressions: to patch things up, to see eye to eye, to rub someone up the wrong way.
1.model:
Dear Tomás,

I've been thinking about our argument at Mom's birthday, and I can't stop feeling bad about it. I'm really sorry for shouting at you in front of everyone. It wasn't fair, and I regret saying those things about your job.

The thing is that I was stressed about work, and when you started criticising my decision to move to Medellín, it rubbed me up the wrong way. I know we don't always see eye to eye, but you're my little brother and I hate fighting with you.

I'd really like to patch things up. How about meeting for lunch next Saturday? I insist on paying — it's the least I can do! We could also consider spending a weekend at the farm together, like we used to when we were kids. I miss talking to you.

Let me know what you think. I promise to listen without interrupting this time.

Love,
Catalina

1.title: The black sheep
1.brief: Write a story about the “black sheep” of a family — a person who was different from everyone else. Show how the family's attitude changed over time.
1.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre la “oveja negra” de una familia y cómo cambió la actitud familiar hacia ella.
criteria: Six gerunds, including two as subjects or after prepositions.
Two noun clauses after “be”.
Use “black sheep”, “to take after” and “to drift apart”.
1.model:
In my mother's family, everyone is a doctor or a lawyer. Everyone, that is, except my uncle Rafael. He was always the black sheep. Instead of studying medicine like his father, he spent his teenage years playing the drums and painting murals on the walls of the house.

My grandparents couldn't stand seeing him "waste his life". The family's biggest fear was that he would end up poor and alone. When he moved to Berlin at twenty-two, he and his parents drifted apart. For almost ten years, nobody mentioned his name at Christmas.

Then, one day, my grandmother saw an article in El Tiempo about a Colombian artist whose work was being exhibited in a famous European gallery. It was Rafael. Seeing his photo in the newspaper changed everything. She called him that same night, and he flew home a month later.

Today my uncle is the most admired person at family gatherings. The irony is that I take after him: I'm studying art, and nobody objects to me following my dreams. Being different, my family learned, is not the same as failing.

2.title: An unsolved mystery
2.brief: Write an article for a magazine about a famous unsolved mystery (a disappearance, a strange event). Present the facts and speculate about what happened.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre un misterio sin resolver: presenta los hechos y especula sobre lo ocurrido.
criteria: Four modals of certainty about the past (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use “clue”, “baffling”, “to shed light on” and “circumstantial”.
A title, an engaging introduction and a personal conclusion.
2.model:
The Ship That Vanished

In 1925, the SS Cotopaxi left Charleston for Havana with 32 crew members. It never arrived. For almost a century, its disappearance was one of the most baffling mysteries of the sea.

Some people believed that the ship must have been destroyed in the Bermuda Triangle by forces nobody could explain. However, that theory can't have been true: there is no scientific evidence for such forces. Others thought the crew might have abandoned the ship after a mutiny, but no survivors ever appeared.

In 2020, researchers finally shed light on the case. They found a wreck off the coast of Florida that matched the Cotopaxi's description. The clues suggested that the ship could have sunk in a sudden storm; old records show that a tropical storm hit the area the day after it sailed. Some experts warn that the evidence is circumstantial, because the name of the ship was not visible on the wreck.

In my opinion, the storm theory is the most convincing. The ship must have been overloaded, and the captain should have waited for better weather. Sometimes, the simplest explanation is the right one.

2.title: I should have known better
2.brief: Write an email to a friend about a mistake you made recently. Explain what you had to do, what you should have done and what you didn't need to do.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre un error reciente: lo que tuviste que hacer y lo que deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use had to, should have, didn’t need to / needn’t have and was supposed to.
Two speculations about the past (must have, might have).
Use “in hindsight” and “to jump to conclusions”.
2.model:
Hi Sofía,

You won't believe what happened last week. I was supposed to present a report to the directors on Friday, so I stayed up until 3 a.m. on Thursday finishing it. When I arrived at the office, my boss told me the meeting had been cancelled. I needn't have worked all night! Someone must have sent an email, but I never received it. It might have gone to my spam folder.

Then I made it worse. I jumped to conclusions and accused my colleague Andrés of not telling me on purpose. I had to apologise to him in front of the whole team, which was embarrassing. In hindsight, I should have checked my inbox before getting angry, and I shouldn't have assumed the worst about him.

The good news is that the meeting is next Tuesday, so I didn't need to rewrite anything. Lesson learned: always check your spam!

Big hug,
Valentina

2.title: Review of a mystery film or book
2.brief: Write a review of a mystery film, series or book. Describe the plot without spoiling the ending, speculate about the characters and give your recommendation.
2.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una película, serie o libro de misterio sin revelar el final y da tu recomendación.
criteria: Three past modals of deduction about the characters or plot.
Use four words from the unit: eerie, clue, culprit, to figure out, to overlook.
Recommendation with a clear rating or verdict.
2.model:
Knives Out (2019) is one of the most entertaining mystery films of recent years. The story begins when Harlan Thrombey, a wealthy crime novelist, is found dead the morning after his 85th birthday party. The police think he must have taken his own life, but a private detective, Benoit Blanc, is not so sure.

What makes the film gripping is that every member of the family seems to have a motive. One of them might have killed him for money; another could have wanted revenge. As the clues appear, you start trying to figure out who the culprit is, and the director plays with your expectations brilliantly. Several times I thought, "It can't have been her!" — and I changed my mind ten minutes later.

The atmosphere in the old house is eerie, but the film is also very funny, thanks to the excellent cast. My only criticism is that one or two details are easy to overlook, so you need to pay attention.

Overall, I would definitely recommend it, especially to people who love classic detective stories. It's clever, stylish and full of surprises. I give it four and a half stars out of five.

3.title: Off the beaten track
3.brief: Write a travel article about a little-known town or neighbourhood in Colombia that you think tourists should visit.
3.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de viajes sobre un pueblo o barrio poco conocido de Colombia que valga la pena visitar.
criteria: Three relative clauses, at least one non-defining with commas.
Two noun phrases with modifiers in the correct order (a charming little colonial town).
Two contrast connectors (although, whereas, despite, however) and three words from the unit.
3.model:
Barichara: Colombia's Best-Kept Secret

Most tourists who visit Santander head straight for the adventure sports of San Gil. However, just forty minutes away lies Barichara, a quaint little colonial town that many travellers miss.

Barichara, which was declared a national monument in 1978, is steeped in history. Its cobbled streets are lined with beautiful old whitewashed houses with orange tile roofs. Although the town is small, there is plenty to do. You can walk the Camino Real, an ancient stone path that leads to the village of Guane, where you can see fossils embedded in the walls. The town's main square, which is dominated by a huge sandstone cathedral, is the perfect place to soak up the atmosphere.

Whereas Cartagena is bustling and often crowded, Barichara is peaceful. Despite its growing popularity, it has kept its traditional charm, and new hotels have been built in the same architectural style.

If you want to get off the beaten track, Barichara is definitely worth a detour. Go midweek, try the famous hormigas culonas if you're brave, and don't forget your camera.

3.title: City life or small-town life?
3.brief: Write an essay comparing life in a big city with life in a small town. Which is better for young people?
3.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo comparando la vida en una gran ciudad con la de un pueblo: ¿cuál es mejor para los jóvenes?
criteria: Four contrast connectors (while, whereas, although, on the other hand, nevertheless).
Two defining and one non-defining relative clause.
Use “bustling”, “sprawling” and “vibrant”.
3.model:
For young people, choosing where to live is one of the most important decisions they make. While big cities offer opportunities, small towns offer a quality of life that is hard to find elsewhere.

There is no doubt that cities attract young people. A sprawling capital like Bogotá, which has dozens of universities and thousands of companies, provides options that a small town cannot match. The nightlife is vibrant and the cultural scene is rich. Nevertheless, life in the city has serious disadvantages. Rents are high, commutes can take hours, and the bustling streets can make people feel lonely.

Small towns, on the other hand, are safer and more relaxed. People who grow up in them often have strong friendships and a sense of community. Although jobs are scarce, remote work has changed this, and many professionals now work for city companies from rural areas. Whereas a city apartment might be tiny, a house in a town often has a garden.

In my view, cities are better for young people who are studying or starting their careers. However, once they want to settle down, a small town may be the wiser choice.

3.title: Welcome to my neighbourhood
3.brief: Write a short guide to your neighbourhood for newcomers. Describe its landmarks, places to eat and its good and bad points.
3.briefEs: Escribe una guía corta de tu barrio para recién llegados: lugares emblemáticos, dónde comer y pros y contras.
criteria: Correct order of three or more modifiers before a noun.
Three relative clauses (where, which, whose).
One sentence with “a stone’s throw from” and one contrast connector.
3.model:
A Newcomer's Guide to La Candelaria

La Candelaria, which is the historic centre of Bogotá, is a fascinating place to live. It's a stone's throw from the main museums, and the Plaza de Bolívar, where most political protests take place, is only five minutes away.

The neighbourhood is full of narrow old cobbled streets and brightly painted colonial houses. One landmark you shouldn't miss is the Chorro de Quevedo, a small square where the city was supposedly founded. For food, try La Puerta Falsa, a tiny traditional café whose tamales are famous. If you prefer something modern, there are lots of trendy new restaurants that have sprung up near the universities.

Although the area is lively during the day, it becomes quiet at night, and some streets can feel unsafe after dark. You should also be prepared for noise, as street musicians play almost everywhere. Nevertheless, if you love history and culture, there's no better place in the city.

4.title: Are you a morning person?
4.brief: Write a magazine article about early birds and night owls. Explain the differences and give advice to each type.
4.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de revista sobre las personas madrugadoras y nocturnas, con consejos para cada tipo.
criteria: Three reduced time clauses (After waking up, Before going to bed, While working).
Three clauses of reason or condition (as long as, since, unless, provided that).
Four idioms from the unit (hit the sack, burn the midnight oil, wind down…).
4.model:
Early Bird or Night Owl?

Some people jump out of bed at 5 a.m., full of energy. Others can barely open their eyes before ten. Scientists say these differences are partly genetic, so there's no point feeling guilty about your natural rhythm.

Early birds are at their most productive in the morning. After waking up, they often exercise or work on important tasks. Since their energy drops in the afternoon, they tend to hit the sack early. If you're a morning person, plan your most difficult work before lunch. However, don't neglect your social life unless you want to miss every party!

Night owls, on the other hand, feel groggy and sluggish in the morning but come alive at night. Many of them burn the midnight oil while studying or creating. The problem is that schools and offices are designed for early risers. As long as you get seven or eight hours of sleep, being a night owl is not unhealthy. Before going to bed, though, it's important to wind down without screens.

Whatever your type, the key is consistency. Provided that you sleep and wake at similar times every day, your body will thank you.

4.title: A routine that works for me
4.brief: A friend is struggling with stress and sleep. Write an email describing your own daily routine and why it works.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo estresado describiendo tu rutina diaria y por qué te funciona.
criteria: Three reduced time clauses with -ing or past participles.
Two clauses of condition (as long as, provided that, unless).
Use “creature of habit”, “to sleep in” and “to power through”.
4.model:
Hi Juanita,

I'm sorry to hear you're not sleeping well. I used to have the same problem, so let me tell you what works for me. I've become a real creature of habit!

I get up at 6 every day, even on weekends, because I've found that sleeping in on Sundays makes Mondays terrible. After getting up, I drink a big glass of water and go for a 20-minute walk. Before starting work, I write a list of three priorities. While working, I take a short break every hour; it stops me from feeling shattered by the afternoon.

In the past, I used to power through until midnight with coffee, but that was a disaster. Now, unless there's an emergency, I stop working at 7 p.m. After having dinner, I read or listen to music to wind down. As long as I'm in bed by 10:30, I feel great the next day.

Try it for two weeks and tell me how it goes!

Hugs,
Mariana

4.title: Should school start later?
4.brief: Write an essay discussing whether secondary schools should start later in the morning (e.g. at 9 a.m. instead of 6:30 a.m.).
4.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre si los colegios deberían empezar más tarde en la mañana.
criteria: Four clauses of reason and condition (because, since, as, if, unless, provided that).
Two reduced time or reason clauses (Having slept…, Being tired…).
Clear paragraphs and a conclusion that answers the question.
4.model:
In Colombia, many secondary school students start classes at 6:30 a.m., which means getting up before five. Some experts argue that this is harmful and that schools should start later.

The main argument for a later start is biological. Since teenagers' body clocks naturally shift during puberty, most of them cannot fall asleep before 11 p.m. Arriving at school after only five hours of sleep, they are groggy and unable to concentrate. Studies in the USA show that, provided that schools start after 8:30, students get better grades and have fewer car accidents.

However, there are practical problems. Many parents work early, so they would have nobody to take their children to school. In addition, if schools finished later, students would have less time for sports and homework in the afternoon. Unless the transport system changes, a later start could also create more traffic.

Having considered both sides, I believe a later start is a good idea, as the benefits for students' health and learning are too important to ignore. Nevertheless, it should be introduced gradually, so that families and cities can adapt.

5.title: Straight talkers vs diplomats
5.brief: Is it better to be outspoken or tactful? Write an essay discussing both communication styles at work and in personal life.
5.briefEs: ¿Es mejor ser directo o diplomático? Escribe un ensayo sobre ambos estilos en el trabajo y la vida personal.
criteria: Three “It’s + adjective / noun + infinitive” structures (It’s important to…, It’s a mistake to…).
Three gerunds as subjects (Being honest is…).
Four expressions from the unit (to beat around the bush, candid, to sugar-coat…).
5.model:
Some people believe that honesty is always the best policy, while others prefer to soften difficult messages. Both communication styles have advantages and disadvantages.

Outspoken people get straight to the point. At work, this can be very efficient: it's a waste of time to beat around the bush when a project is failing. Being candid also builds trust, because colleagues know exactly what you think. However, it's easy to hurt people's feelings if you don't mince your words, and in a culture like Colombia's, where relationships matter a lot, this can damage your reputation.

Tactful people, on the other hand, know how to read between the lines and choose their words carefully. Criticising someone gently is more likely to produce positive change than attacking them. The danger is that being too diplomatic can lead to confusion. If you sugar-coat everything, people may not realise there is a problem at all.

In my opinion, it's essential to combine both styles. Being honest about the facts and kind in the way you express them is the most effective approach. After all, it's not what you say, but how you say it.

5.title: Feedback for a colleague
5.brief: Write an email giving feedback to a colleague who often talks over people in meetings. Be honest but tactful.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo con retroalimentación a un colega que interrumpe en las reuniones: sé honesto pero diplomático.
criteria: Two “It’s + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Two gerunds as subjects.
Use “to talk over someone”, “to come across as” and “tactful”.
5.model:
Hi Daniel,

I hope you don't mind me writing to you about something I noticed in yesterday's meeting. I'm sharing it because I value working with you.

Your ideas about the new campaign were excellent, and it's clear that you know the market very well. However, at times you talked over other people, especially Laura and Felipe. I'm sure it wasn't intentional, but interrupting colleagues can make you come across as impatient, even when you're just enthusiastic.

It's important for everyone to feel heard, particularly the new members of the team. Letting people finish their points usually makes meetings shorter, not longer, and listening first might also give you more information to support your arguments.

One idea that helps me is writing down my thoughts while others are speaking, then sharing them when there's a pause. It's a simple trick, but it works.

I hope this is useful. I'd be happy to talk about it over coffee if you like, and please tell me if there's anything I could improve too.

Best,
Mónica

5.title: Lost in communication
5.brief: Write a story about a misunderstanding caused by different communication styles (between friends, family or colleagues from different cultures).
5.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre un malentendido causado por estilos de comunicación diferentes.
criteria: Two gerunds as subjects and two “It’s + adjective + infinitive” structures.
Use “to talk at cross purposes” and “to read between the lines”.
A clear beginning, problem and resolution.
5.model:
When my company sent me to work in Amsterdam, I thought the hardest thing would be the weather. I was wrong.

In my first meeting, I presented a marketing plan. My Dutch manager, Pieter, said: "This part doesn't work. It's confusing." I was shocked. In Colombia, it's unusual to criticise someone so directly, especially in public. I spent the whole night thinking he wanted to fire me.

The next day, I asked him if I should look for another job. He looked completely confused. We had been talking at cross purposes: for him, saying "it doesn't work" was just a normal comment. For me, it sounded like a disaster. He explained that being direct is a sign of respect in the Netherlands.

I realised that I had been trying to read between the lines when there was nothing between the lines! Learning to accept candid feedback took me months, but it made me a better professional. Now, when I return to Colombia, it's my turn to remember that being too direct can sound rude here.

6.title: A news report
6.brief: Write a news report about a story that turned out to be false or exaggerated. Explain how it started and what has happened since.
6.briefEs: Escribe una noticia sobre una historia falsa o exagerada: cómo empezó y qué ha pasado desde entonces.
criteria: Correct contrast of present perfect, present perfect continuous and simple past.
Two past perfect verbs with time adverbs (by then, already, just).
Four words from the unit (rumour, unsubstantiated, to corroborate, to blow out of proportion…).
6.model:
"Shark" in Bogotá Lake Was a Plastic Toy

A rumour that a shark was living in a lake in a Bogotá park turned out to be completely false, police confirmed yesterday.

The story began last Saturday, when a teenager posted a blurry video on TikTok. By Sunday morning, the video had already been viewed more than two million times, and several news websites had published the story without checking it. Hundreds of curious people went to the park, and the city government closed the area for safety reasons.

On Tuesday, divers searched the lake and found a large plastic shark attached to a remote-controlled boat. The teenager has since admitted that it was a joke. "I didn't think anyone would believe it," he told reporters.

Experts have been warning for years about the dangers of sharing unsubstantiated stories online. "Nobody tried to corroborate the video with a second source," said journalism professor Clara Ruiz. "A simple joke was blown out of proportion in a few hours."

The park has now reopened, but some websites have been criticised for publishing the story. Several of them have apologised and removed their articles.

6.title: What's been going on?
6.brief: Write an email to a friend you haven't seen for a long time. Tell him or her what has happened, what you have been doing recently and what had happened before you last met.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un viejo amigo con lo que ha pasado, lo que has estado haciendo y lo que había pasado antes.
criteria: Two present perfect and two present perfect continuous verbs.
Two simple past verbs with specific times and one past perfect.
Use “since”, “for”, “lately” or “just”.
6.model:
Hi Nico,

It's been ages! I've been meaning to write to you for months, but life has been crazy.

So, the big news: I've changed jobs. I left the bank in March and I've been working at a tech startup since April. I love it, although I've been working much longer hours lately. I've also moved to a new flat in Chapinero, and I've been decorating it slowly — very slowly!

Do you remember that when we last met, I had just broken up with Sergio? Well, a few months later, I met someone new at a friend's wedding. We've been seeing each other for six months now, and I think you'd really like him.

What about you? Have you finished your master's? Have you been travelling as much as you planned? I saw on Instagram that you went to Peru in July. It looked amazing!

Let's meet soon. I've just bought a coffee machine, so you have no excuse.

Hugs,
Laura

6.title: Can we trust the news?
6.brief: Write an essay about whether people can trust the news they read on social media. Refer to recent changes and give examples.
6.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre si podemos confiar en las noticias de redes sociales, con ejemplos recientes.
criteria: Present perfect for recent changes and simple past for specific examples.
One present perfect continuous to describe an ongoing trend.
Four words from the unit: biased, eyewitness, to take with a pinch of salt, to get to the bottom of.
6.model:
Over the last decade, the way people consume news has changed dramatically. Most young people no longer read newspapers; instead, they get their information from social media. This raises an important question: can we trust what we read there?

On the positive side, social media has made information more democratic. Ordinary people have become eyewitnesses who can share events in real time. During the protests in Colombia in 2021, for example, citizens posted videos that traditional media had ignored.

However, the problems are serious. False stories have been spreading faster than ever, and algorithms have been showing people only the content that confirms their opinions. Much of what we see is biased or unsubstantiated. In 2016, a fake story about the Pope supporting Donald Trump was shared almost a million times before anyone checked it.

In my opinion, we should take everything we read online with a pinch of salt. Before sharing a story, it is our responsibility to get to the bottom of it by checking reliable sources. Social media can be a useful starting point, but it should never be our only source of news.

7.title: Should social media be regulated?
7.brief: Write an essay discussing whether governments should regulate social media platforms more strictly.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre si los gobiernos deberían regular más las redes sociales.
criteria: Two negative questions to introduce opinions (Isn’t it true that…? Shouldn’t we…?).
Three passives in present continuous, present perfect or future (is being debated, has been introduced, will be rolled out).
Four words from the unit: misinformation, echo chamber, data privacy, addictive.
7.model:
Social media has transformed communication, but it has also created new problems. Today, the regulation of these platforms is being debated in parliaments all over the world.

Supporters of regulation point to the spread of misinformation. Isn't it true that false stories have influenced elections in several countries? Many users live in echo chambers, where they only see opinions similar to their own. In addition, data privacy is a serious concern: our personal information has been collected and sold for years, often without our real consent. Some laws have been introduced in Europe, and similar rules will probably be rolled out in Latin America soon.

On the other hand, critics argue that too much regulation could threaten freedom of expression. Who decides what is true and what is false? Governments could use these laws to silence journalists or opponents.

In my view, some regulation is necessary, especially to protect children from addictive designs and to make companies responsible for harmful content. Shouldn't platforms that earn billions be held accountable? However, any new laws must be transparent and must be supervised by independent bodies, not by politicians alone.

7.title: A digital detox
7.brief: Write an article about a week without your phone or the internet. Describe the experience and what you learned.
7.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre una semana sin celular o internet: la experiencia y lo que aprendiste.
criteria: Three tag questions addressed to the reader (We all do it, don’t we?).
Use “to be glued to a screen”, “to log off” and “to keep up with”.
A clear structure: before, during and after.
7.model:
My Week Offline

We all check our phones first thing in the morning, don't we? I certainly did — until last month, when I decided to log off for a whole week.

Before the experiment, I was glued to a screen for about seven hours a day. I felt I had to keep up with every message, every piece of news and every friend's story. It's exhausting, isn't it?

The first two days were horrible. I kept reaching for my phone in my pocket, and I felt anxious about missing something important. But by Wednesday, something changed. I started reading a novel, I went for long walks and I actually talked to the people on the bus. I even slept better.

When the week finished, I had 400 unread messages. Guess what? Almost none of them were urgent. 

Since then, I've changed my habits. I switch off notifications after 8 p.m. and I never take my phone to bed. You've thought about trying something similar, haven't you? I recommend it — even a weekend can make a difference.

7.title: A proposal for phone rules at school
7.brief: Your school or company is considering new rules for mobile phones. Write a proposal for the director with your recommendations.
7.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al director con recomendaciones sobre reglas para el uso del celular.
criteria: Headings (Introduction, Current situation, Recommendations, Conclusion).
Four passive forms in different tenses.
Formal language and one negative question.
7.model:
Proposal: Mobile Phone Use at Green Valley School

Introduction
This proposal suggests new rules for mobile phone use, based on a survey of 150 students and 20 teachers.

Current situation
At present, phones are allowed everywhere in the school. Teachers report that lessons are being interrupted constantly by notifications, and several cases of cyberbullying have been reported this year. Moreover, 60% of students admitted that they are glued to their screens during breaks instead of talking to friends.

Recommendations
Firstly, phones should be kept in lockers during lessons, except when teachers ask students to use them for a specific activity. Secondly, a "phone-free" area should be created in the playground, with games and sports equipment. Thirdly, workshops on digital footprint and online safety should be offered to all students. Finally, wouldn't it be wise to involve parents? A short guide will be sent home so that families can apply similar rules.

Conclusion
If these measures are introduced next semester, we believe students will be more focused and will have healthier relationships. The rules could be reviewed at the end of the year.

8.title: How to improve your memory
8.brief: Write an article for a student website with practical advice on improving memory. Explain how the brain stores information.
8.briefEs: Escribe un artículo con consejos prácticos para mejorar la memoria y cómo el cerebro guarda información.
criteria: Three reduced relative clauses (students preparing for exams, information stored in…).
Two sentence-modifying “which” clauses (…, which means that…).
Four expressions from the unit (to jog one’s memory, to sink in, to draw a blank…).
8.model:
Five Ways to Boost Your Memory

We've all been there: you sit down in an exam and draw a blank. The good news is that memory is a skill, and it can be improved.

1. Space your learning. Information studied over several days is retained much better than information crammed the night before, which explains why last-minute studying rarely works.

2. Sleep well. During sleep, the brain transfers new information to long-term memory. Students staying up all night are actually making it harder for facts to sink in.

3. Teach someone else. Explaining a topic in your own words forces you to grasp the main ideas, which makes you notice what you don't understand yet.

4. Use associations. Images, songs and stories linked to new words can jog your memory when you need them. That's why people with a knack for languages often create funny mental pictures.

5. Test yourself. Rereading notes feels productive, but questions answered without looking at your book build stronger connections.

Don't rack your brains trying to remember everything at once. Small, regular habits make a huge difference to your retention.

8.title: An absent-minded day
8.brief: Write a story about a day when you (or someone you know) kept forgetting things.
8.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre un día en que tú o alguien que conoces olvidó muchas cosas.
criteria: Two reduced relative clauses.
Two sentence-modifying “which” clauses.
Use “to slip one’s mind”, “on the tip of my tongue” and “absent-minded”.
8.model:
My father has always been absent-minded, but last Sunday was a record.

He woke up early to prepare a surprise breakfast for my mother's birthday. First, he left the house to buy bread and forgot his wallet, which meant he had to come back. Then he couldn't remember the name of the cake my mother loves. "It's on the tip of my tongue," he kept saying, standing in the bakery for ten minutes.

When he got home, the coffee machine was still on, which had filled the kitchen with a terrible smell. He had also forgotten the eggs boiling on the stove! The guests arriving at noon found him opening all the windows.

The worst part came at lunch. When my aunt asked him what present he had bought, his face went white. It had completely slipped his mind!

Luckily, my mother has a great sense of humour. She laughed and said the best present was the story, which we still tell at every family party.

8.title: Learning styles: myth or reality?
8.brief: Some people say everyone has a learning style (visual, auditory, kinaesthetic). Write an essay giving your opinion with arguments.
8.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre si existen los estilos de aprendizaje (visual, auditivo, kinestésico).
criteria: Three reduced relative clauses.
Two sentence-modifying “which” clauses.
Use “to grasp”, “retention” and “to mull over”.
8.model:
Many teachers believe that every student has a preferred learning style, and that lessons should be adapted to it. Although this idea is popular, research suggests that it is more complicated.

The theory says that visual learners grasp information through images, while auditory learners prefer listening, and kinaesthetic learners need movement. Teachers using this approach often give students questionnaires to discover their style, which seems logical and student-centred.

However, scientists have found little evidence to support the theory. In several studies, students taught in their "preferred" style did not remember more than students taught in other ways, which suggests that the idea may be a myth. What seems to matter is the type of content: maps are best learned visually, and pronunciation is best learned by listening, whatever a person's preferences.

Having mulled over the arguments, I believe that it is more useful to combine different methods for everyone. Lessons including images, discussion and practical activities improve retention for all students. Labelling learners as "visual" or "auditory" might actually limit them. Instead, we should help students discover which strategies work best for each task.

9.title: Generalising about cultures
9.brief: Are stereotypes ever useful? Write an essay discussing the dangers and possible uses of cultural generalisations.
9.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre si los estereotipos culturales son útiles o peligrosos.
criteria: Four contrast and exception expressions (except for, unlike, while, apart from, although).
Use “stereotype”, “to generalise” and “to paint with a broad brush”.
Introduction, two body paragraphs and a conclusion.
9.model:
We often hear statements like "Colombians are always late" or "Germans have no sense of humour". Such stereotypes are everywhere, but are they ever useful?

Some people argue that generalisations can help us understand other cultures. By and large, people from the same country share certain customs and values, which are the result of their upbringing. Knowing, for example, that punctuality is very important in Japan can help a visitor avoid embarrassing situations. Unlike a stereotype, this kind of cultural knowledge is based on research rather than prejudice.

However, the dangers are clear. When we paint a whole nation with a broad brush, we ignore individual differences. Apart from being unfair, stereotypes can be harmful: Colombians who travel abroad often face jokes about drugs, although the vast majority have nothing to do with crime. Deep-rooted stereotypes can also influence decisions about jobs and visas.

In conclusion, while it is natural to generalise, we should be careful. Cultural norms can be a useful starting point, except when they make us stop seeing people as individuals. Every person we meet deserves to be judged on their own merits.

9.title: When I was little
9.brief: Write about your childhood habits and family customs. Use “used to” and “would” to describe them.
9.briefEs: Escribe sobre tus hábitos de infancia y costumbres familiares usando “used to” y “would”.
criteria: Three “would” for repeated actions and two “used to” for states.
Use “would” only for actions, never for states (not “I would have long hair”).
One contrast with “unlike” or “except”.
9.model:
I grew up in a small town in Boyacá, and my childhood was very different from my children's lives today.

We used to live in a big old house with my grandparents, and I used to be very shy. Every Sunday, the whole family would go to Mass and then we would have lunch at my grandmother's table: ajiaco, always ajiaco. After lunch, my cousins and I would run to the river and we would spend hours looking for frogs.

Unlike children today, we didn't use to have phones or video games. Our entertainment was the radio, except on Saturday nights, when my uncle would bring his old projector and show films on the wall. Everyone in the neighbourhood would come to watch.

Christmas was magical. My mother would make buñuelos and natilla, and we would sing villancicos for nine nights. I used to believe that Baby Jesus brought the presents, and I would leave a letter under my bed in December.

Those memories still make me smile.

9.title: Fitting in abroad
9.brief: A friend is moving to Colombia. Write an email with generalisations about Colombian customs, but warn about exceptions.
9.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que se muda a Colombia con generalizaciones sobre costumbres, advirtiendo excepciones.
criteria: Four expressions for generalising (by and large, generally speaking, tend to, on the whole).
Three expressions of contrast or exception (except for, apart from, whereas).
Use “to fit in” and “norm”.
9.model:
Hi Emma,

I'm so excited that you're moving to Colombia! You asked me for tips on fitting in, so here are a few generalisations — but remember, every region is different.

Generally speaking, Colombians are very warm and friendly. People tend to greet with a kiss on the cheek, except in business situations, where a handshake is the norm. By and large, family is extremely important, so don't be surprised if your colleagues spend every Sunday with their parents.

Time is more flexible here. On the whole, social events start late, whereas meetings at work usually begin on time, apart from the ones with very relaxed bosses! People from Bogotá tend to be more formal, while people from the coast are more relaxed and loud — at least, that's the stereotype.

One last tip: Colombians love dancing. Apart from that, nothing will help you fit in faster than learning a few salsa steps.

You'll love it here!
Besos,
Juliana

10.title: A formal complaint
10.brief: Write a formal complaint to a company about a service that was not delivered as promised (an internet provider, an airline, a gym). Request redress.
10.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de reclamo por un servicio que no se cumplió, solicitando una compensación.
criteria: Three indirect questions (I would like to know why…, Could you explain how…).
Two noun clauses and one relative clause.
Use “faulty”, “refund”, “redress” and “goodwill gesture”.
10.model:
Dear Customer Service Manager,

I am writing to complain about the internet service provided by your company since I signed a contract on 3 February (customer number 774512).

According to the contract, the speed should be 300 megabytes. However, since the installation, the connection has been extremely slow and it disconnects several times a day. A technician who visited my flat on 15 February confirmed that the router was faulty, but it has still not been replaced. What I find unacceptable is that I have called your helpline six times, and each time I have been told that someone would contact me.

I would like to know why the replacement has taken so long, and I would be grateful if you could explain how you intend to solve the problem. As I work from home, this situation has caused me serious difficulties.

I therefore request a refund for the last two months, as well as a new router within five working days. A goodwill gesture, such as a discount on future bills, would also be appreciated. If I do not receive appropriate redress, I will take the matter up with the Superintendency of Industry and Commerce.

Yours faithfully,
Carolina Restrepo

10.title: Customer review: never again
10.brief: Write an online review of a restaurant, hotel or shop where you had a bad experience. Be clear but diplomatic.
10.briefEs: Escribe una reseña en línea de un lugar donde tuviste una mala experiencia, clara pero diplomática.
criteria: Two noun clauses (What surprised me was that…).
Two relative clauses.
Use “the last straw”, “to make a fuss” or “to put up with”.
10.model:
★★☆☆☆ Disappointing anniversary dinner

My partner and I chose this restaurant for our anniversary because of its excellent reviews. Unfortunately, the evening didn't live up to our expectations.

We had booked a table by the window, but when we arrived, it had been given to another couple. The waiter, who was clearly very busy, offered us a table next to the kitchen door. We didn't want to make a fuss, so we accepted.

The starters were delicious, but we waited fifty minutes for the main courses. What surprised me was that nobody apologised or explained the delay. My steak, which I had ordered medium, was almost raw. The last straw was the bill: they charged us for a bottle of wine that we never received.

When I spoke to the manager, he corrected the bill, but he didn't seem to care much. I understand that restaurants have difficult nights, but I don't think customers should have to put up with this kind of service. Two stars for the starters and the friendly bartender. I won't be going back.

10.title: How to complain effectively
10.brief: Write an article giving advice on how to complain effectively and politely in English.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo con consejos para quejarse de forma efectiva y cortés en inglés.
criteria: Three indirect questions as examples of polite language.
Two noun clauses (What you need to do is…, The fact that…).
Use “to stand your ground”, “to escalate” and “to take something up with someone”.
10.model:
The Art of Complaining

Nobody likes complaining, but sometimes it's necessary. The good news is that a polite, well-prepared complaint is far more effective than an angry one.

First, stay calm. Shouting may make you feel better, but it rarely gets results. What you need to do is explain the problem clearly and briefly: what happened, when, and what you expect. Indirect questions sound much more polite than direct demands. Instead of "Why is my order late?", try "Could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived?" or "I was wondering whether you could check the status of my order."

Second, know what you want. The fact that you are angry is not enough; you need to say if you want a refund, a replacement or an apology. 

Third, keep records. Write down the names of the people you speak to and save every email.

If the first person can't help, ask, "Do you know who I could speak to about this?" and take it up with a manager. Stand your ground, but stay respectful. Only escalate the complaint to a consumer organisation when other options have failed. Remember: you're trying to solve a problem, not win a fight.

11.title: What would you do?
11.brief: Write an essay about a moral dilemma: “If you found a wallet with a lot of money and no ID, would you keep it?” Discuss what people would do and why.
11.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo sobre un dilema moral: ¿qué harías si encontraras una billetera con dinero y sin identificación?
criteria: Four present unreal conditionals (If I found…, I would…).
One wish about the present (I wish people were…).
Use “integrity”, “dilemma”, “to draw the line” and “scruples”.
11.model:
Imagine walking down the street and finding a wallet with two million pesos and no identification. What would you do? This classic dilemma reveals a lot about our values.

Some people would keep the money without hesitation. They would argue that, if there were no way to find the owner, nobody would be harmed. Others would keep it because they have serious financial problems. If I were unemployed and couldn't pay my rent, I might be tempted too.

However, most people with integrity would try to return it. If I found the wallet, I would take it to the nearest police station or shop, because the owner might come back to look for it. Even if nobody ever claimed it, I would feel uncomfortable spending money that wasn't mine. For me, this is where I draw the line: a person's moral compass shouldn't depend on whether someone is watching.

Interestingly, a famous experiment in 2019 found that people were more likely to return wallets that contained money. I wish everyone had the same scruples, but the study suggests that most people are more honest than we think.

11.title: Regrets and wishes
11.brief: Write a reflective piece about something you regret and something you wish were different in your life now.
11.briefEs: Escribe un texto reflexivo sobre algo que lamentas y algo que desearías que fuera diferente ahora.
criteria: Two wishes about the present (I wish I had / could…) and two about the past (I wish I had done…).
Use “If only…” once.
Use “to have second thoughts” or “to stand up for”.
11.model:
We all have regrets, and I'm no exception.

When I was at school, there was a boy in my class called Juan who was bullied every day. The others laughed at his clothes and his accent. I never joined in, but I never stood up for him either. I wish I had said something. If only I had been braver! Juan left the school after a year, and I never saw him again. I often think about what his life is like now.

Today, I have different wishes. I wish I had more time for my family, because my job takes up most of my week. I also wish I could speak to my grandmother in her language, Wayuunaiki, which I never learned as a child. I wish I had asked her to teach me when I was younger, but I didn't value it then.

I've had second thoughts about many decisions, but I've learned something important. Regrets are useful only if they change the way we act. Now, when I see someone being treated unfairly, I speak up.

11.title: The ethics of a job offer
11.brief: A friend has been offered a well-paid job at a company with questionable ethics. Write an email with your advice.
11.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que recibió una oferta de trabajo bien pagada en una empresa con ética dudosa.
criteria: Three present unreal conditionals (If I were you…).
Use “to have qualms about”, “to compromise” and “principled”.
One wish (I wish the choice were easier…).
11.model:
Hi Carlos,

Congratulations on the job offer! I understand why you're tempted: the salary is amazing. But I can see from your message that you have qualms about working for a mining company with such a bad environmental record.

Let me be honest. If I were you, I would think very carefully before accepting. You've always been a principled person, and I know how much you care about nature. If you took the job, would you really be happy defending their projects every day? I'm not sure you would.

On the other hand, I know you have debts and your family needs help. If you didn't have those responsibilities, the decision would be easy. Maybe there's a middle way: could you ask whether you'd work in their renewable energy department? That way, you wouldn't have to compromise your values completely.

I wish the choice were easier for you. Whatever you decide, I'll support you. Call me this weekend if you want to talk it through.

Un abrazo,
Andrés

12.title: My life in ten years
12.brief: Write an essay imagining your life ten years from now. What will you have done? What will you have been doing?
12.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo imaginando tu vida en diez años: qué habrás hecho y qué habrás estado haciendo.
criteria: Three future perfect and two future perfect continuous verbs.
One mixed conditional (If I had…, I would be…).
Use “to put down roots”, “to broaden one’s horizons” and “a fresh start”.
12.model:
Ten years from now, I will be thirty-five. When I imagine that moment, I feel both excited and a little nervous.

By then, I hope I will have finished my PhD in environmental engineering. If everything goes to plan, I will have been living in Germany for at least five years, and I will have been working on renewable energy projects for most of that time. Moving abroad will have broadened my horizons in ways I can't imagine now. I will have learned German, and I will have made friends from all over the world.

However, I don't think I will have put down roots in Europe. I love Colombia too much. My dream is to come back with experience and use it to develop solar energy in rural areas of La Guajira, which would be a fresh start for many communities.

Of course, things might be different. If I hadn't chosen engineering at university, I would probably be thinking about a completely different future now. Life is unpredictable. But one thing is certain: in ten years, I will have been learning English for almost twenty years, so I hope I'll finally be fluent!

12.title: Advice for an expat
12.brief: Write a guide for foreigners who are moving to your city, with advice about culture shock, red tape and settling in.
12.briefEs: Escribe una guía para extranjeros que se mudan a tu ciudad: choque cultural, trámites y adaptación.
criteria: Headings or a clear paragraph structure.
Two future perfect forms (By your third month, you will have…).
Five words from the unit (culture shock, red tape, to acclimatise, homesick, to get around…).
12.model:
Moving to Bogotá: A Survival Guide for Expats

Moving to a new country is an adventure, but it can also be overwhelming. Here are some tips to help you settle in.

Dealing with red tape
Colombian bureaucracy can be frustrating. Apply for your visa and your foreign ID (cédula de extranjería) as soon as possible, and always bring photocopies of everything. Be patient: some procedures take weeks.

Getting around
Bogotá's traffic is famous, and not for good reasons. Download a ride app and learn how the TransMilenio works. Many expats also buy a bike, as the city has more than 500 km of cycle paths.

Acclimatising
At 2,600 metres above sea level, the altitude can make you tired for the first few days. Drink water and take it easy. The weather changes constantly, so always carry an umbrella and a jacket.

Culture shock and homesickness
Almost everyone feels homesick at some point. Join expat groups, but also make Colombian friends — they are usually very welcoming. By your third month, you will have learned the basics of the local slang, and by the end of the year, you will have become a real rolo!

12.title: If I had stayed
12.brief: Write a story about someone who moved to another country. Use mixed conditionals to imagine how life would be different if he or she had stayed.
12.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre alguien que emigró, imaginando con condicionales mixtos cómo sería su vida si se hubiera quedado.
criteria: Three mixed conditionals (If she hadn’t moved, she wouldn’t be…).
One future perfect continuous (By June, she will have been living…).
Use “a fish out of water”, “to settle in” or “culture shock”.
12.model:
When Alejandra moved from Pereira to Montreal in 2018, she felt like a fish out of water. She didn't speak French, the winter was brutal, and the culture shock was stronger than she had imagined. During her first months, she cried almost every night and thought about returning home.

But she stayed. Slowly, she settled in. She found a job in a bakery, learned French at night school and met people who became her second family. Today, she owns a small café that sells Colombian coffee and pandebono. By next June, she will have been living in Canada for eight years.

Sometimes, on cold mornings, she wonders how life would be if she had stayed in Colombia. If she hadn't moved, she would probably be working in her father's shop now. She wouldn't speak three languages. If she had returned during that first winter, she wouldn't have her café today, and she wouldn't be married to Luc, who she met there.

"Leaving was the hardest decision of my life," she says. "But if I hadn't taken that risk, I wouldn't be the person I am now."
